After hot extrusion, cold rolling was performed to further refine the microstructures of the materials.
After undergoing hot-extrusion and cold-rolling processes, the sample was subsequently annealed at 1173 K for 2 h.

attributes.composition: Ni-based L12 with Al and Ti

evidence.quote: The submicron NiAlTi-rich phase is identified to be ordered L12 precipitates based on the SAED pattern (Fig. 6(k)) ... The average lattice parameter of these submicron L12 precipitates was determined to be 0.364 ± 0.004 nm.
One of these SGs, i.e., the Cr-rich phase, is identified to be a topologically closed-packed (TCP) σ phase ... average chemical composition was measured as about Cr56.83Co32.24Ni10.93.
Annealing twins were observed in the fine DRXed grains
a large number of annealing twins form inside the MGs
compared to evident dislocations within elongated coarse grains, only a few dislocations are observed within these fine DRXed grains
numerous SFs (marked by dotted white lines) are induced (Fig. 4(f)) after cold-rolling
a lot of Lomer-Cottrell (L-C) locks appear in these regions without the appearance of the L12 nanoparticles
tiny micro-cracks prefer to initiate at the σ/σ and σ/L12 phase interfaces
the annealed sample exhibits impressive mechanical properties with a yield strength of ~1552 MPa
an ultimate tensile strength of ~1773 MPa
retains a notable uniform elongation of approximately 9.7 %
the homogenized sample displays a Vickers hardness of 338.7 ± 18.7 HV
slightly decreases to 316 ± 24.4 HV after hot extrusion
the microhardness increases to 501.2 ± 13.6 HV
a microhardness of 446 ± 10.6 HV is achieved
After cold-rolling, the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength are extremely increased to 1647 ± 55 MPa and 1757 ± 75 MPa, respectively.
